html:
SMTO-BOOT-0036 — The model server stopped while it was starting

GUID: 0b27454f-70af-407c-bbcd-d0b6977bfe36
Slug: boot-model-process-exited
Domain: BOOT · Subsystem: boot

What happened

  • The benchmark started a model server, but that server closed before it was ready. This model gets no score in the report, and the benchmark moves on to the next one.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. Open the log file named in the message (it's in src/vllm/results/ and ends in .server.log) and read the last 20 lines. The model server writes the reason it closed there; the benchmark only sees that it stopped.
  2. If the log mentions running out of memory, run the benchmark again for just this model with a smaller context, for example by putting MAX_MODEL_LEN=16384 in front of the command. The model didn't fit in the graphics card's memory, and a smaller context than the model's start script uses needs less of it.
  3. If the log says vllm can't be found or imported, run ./src/vllm/install-vllm.sh --verify-only vllm to check the model environment. The benchmark runs inside that environment, and a missing or broken install makes the server close at once.
  4. If the log shows a download error, check this computer's internet connection and free disk space, then try again. The first start downloads the model's files, and the server stops if that download fails.

What success looks like

  • The benchmark gets past startup for that model and the report shows a score for it.

If it still fails

  • Send this model's section of the benchmark report and its .server.log file to the person who maintains your model setup. Don't delete the model download folder to fix this; it only forces a long download again.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The benchmark's launched start-script process exited before /v1/models reported the profile's model, so the profile failed startup.

What this means

  • Benchmark launch observes its owned subprocess has exited before a successful readiness result. Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.

Why this can happen

  • Benchmark launch observes its owned subprocess has exited before a successful readiness result.

How to diagnose it

  • Read the exact profile's captured server log and exit evidence.

How to fix it

  • Read the launcher log named in the message (the profile's .server.log in src/vllm/results/) for the exit cause: CUDA out of memory (set MAX_MODEL_LEN below the start script's default first, then GPU_MEMORY_UTILIZATION; the start scripts read both from the environment), a failed weight download into HF_HOME (default ~/models/data), or vllm missing from the active Conda environment (check with ./src/vllm/install-vllm.sh --verify-only vllm). Correct that cause and rerun only that profile with --models.
  • Inspect the named launcher log and correct its startup failure.

Retry and execution caution

  • Correct the recorded cause, then inspect current state and existing receipts before requesting another attempt.

How to verify the fix

  • A corrected owned launch stays alive through readiness.

What not to do

  • Do not remove retained state or weaken trust checks to make an unavailable dependency appear healthy.

Technical notes

  • Bootstrap diagnostics report the existing installer/launcher check only. They do not download packages, probe hardware, stop processes or change state while rendering; earlier setup steps may already have modified the environment.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
